## Plots


```{r}
mytheme <- theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#2B6082", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12, margin = margin(b = 15)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), # Remove vertical grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) 
```


### Column chart

```{r}
ggplot(gdp_est_cagr, 
        aes(x = indicators, y = cagr, fill = period)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", cagr)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
            vjust = -0.5,
            size = 3, 
            #fontface = "bold", 
            color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
                   "2004-2015" = "#B0C4DE", 
                   "2016-2024" = "#31708F")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("Real\nExports","Exports\nin USD",
                            "Domestic\nCredit","Electricity\nGeneration",
                            "Tax\nrevenue", "GDP"
                            )) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Growth rate of macro indicators",
    subtitle = "Annual average growth (percent)",
    x = NULL, 
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + mytheme
```

## Cross country evidence

## Indian data


### 1995 to 2011

#### Data prep

```{r}
df_1995_2011 <- panel_gdp %>%
  # Keep based on conditions
  filter(
    oil_producer == 0,
    small_1995 == 0,
    fragile_state == 0,
    year >= 1995 & year <= 2011
  ) %>%
  # Keep only complete cases for the required variables
  drop_na(
    gdp_growth, export_vol_growth, import_vol_growth, 
    energy_consumption_growth, real_credit_growth, real_tax_growth
  ) %>%
  # Collapse to cross-section (mean by country)
  group_by(country_name) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      c(gdp_growth, export_vol_growth, import_vol_growth, 
        real_credit_growth, energy_consumption_growth, real_tax_growth, india),
      ~ mean(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

#### Regression

```{r}
mod1 <- lm(
  gdp_growth ~ export_vol_growth + import_vol_growth + real_credit_growth + 
               energy_consumption_growth + real_tax_growth + india, 
  data = df_1995_2011
)

# 3. Predicted values and removing India effect
india_coef <- coef(mod1)["india"]

df_1995_2011 <- df_1995_2011 %>%
  mutate(
    yhat = predict(mod1),
    yhat_noindia = yhat - (india_coef * india)
  )

# 4. Second Regression (Actual vs Predicted)
mod2 <- lm(gdp_growth ~ yhat_noindia, data = df_1995_2011)

# 5. Predictions, Standard Errors, and Confidence Intervals
pred2 <- predict(mod2, se.fit = TRUE)

df_1995_2011 <- df_1995_2011 %>%
  mutate(
    fit = pred2$fit,
    sefit = pred2$se.fit,
    ub = fit + qnorm(0.975) * sefit, # qnorm(0.975) is R's invnormal(0.975)
    lb = fit - qnorm(0.975) * sefit
  )

glimpse(df_1995_2011)
```



#### Plotting


```{r}
# 6. Plotting
# Stata RGB colors converted directly to R's rgb() function for exact matching
plot_1995_2011 <- ggplot(df_1995_2011, aes(x = yhat_noindia)) +
  # Confidence Interval (rarea)
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lb, ymax = ub), fill = rgb(186, 181, 213, maxColorValue = 255)) +
  # Fitted Line (line fit)
  geom_line(aes(y = fit), color = rgb(70, 55, 183, maxColorValue = 255), linewidth = 1) +
  # India Point (scatter)
  geom_point(data = filter(df_1995_2011, india == 1), 
             aes(y = gdp_growth), 
             shape = 1, size = 4, color = "blue", stroke = 1.2) +
  # India Label (mlabel)
  geom_text(data = filter(df_1995_2011, india == 1), 
            aes(y = gdp_growth, label = "India"), 
            hjust = -0.3, color = "black", size = 5) +
  # Labels and Theme
  labs(x = "Predicted Growth", y = "Actual Growth") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = rgb(242, 242, 242, maxColorValue = 255), color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

plot_1995_2011

```


### 2012 to 2024

#### Data prep

```{r}
df_2012_2024 <- df %>%
  filter(
    oil_producer == 0,
    small_2011 == 0, 
    fragile_state == 0,
    year >= 2012 & year <= 2024,
    !year %in% c(2020, 2021) 
  ) %>%
  drop_na(
    gdp_growth, export_vol_growth, import_vol_growth, 
    energy_consumption_growth, real_credit_growth, real_tax_growth
  ) %>%
  group_by(country_name) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      c(gdp_growth, export_vol_growth, import_vol_growth, 
        real_credit_growth, energy_consumption_growth, real_tax_growth, india),
      ~ mean(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```


```{r}

mod3 <- lm(
  gdp_growth ~ export_vol_growth + import_vol_growth + real_credit_growth + 
               energy_consumption_growth + real_tax_growth + india, 
  data = df_2012_2024
)

# 3. Predicted values and removing India effect
india_coef_2 <- coef(mod3)["india"]

df_2012_2024 <- df_2012_2024 %>%
  mutate(
    yhat = predict(mod3),
    yhat_noindia = yhat - (india_coef_2 * india)
  )

# 4. Second Regression (Actual vs Predicted)
mod4 <- lm(gdp_growth ~ yhat_noindia, data = df_2012_2024)

# 5. Predictions, Standard Errors, and Confidence Intervals
pred4 <- predict(mod4, se.fit = TRUE)

df_2012_2024 <- df_2012_2024 %>%
  mutate(
    fit = pred4$fit,
    sefit = pred4$se.fit,
    ub = fit + qnorm(0.975) * sefit,
    lb = fit - qnorm(0.975) * sefit
  )

# 6. Plotting
plot_2012_2024 <- ggplot(df_2012_2024, aes(x = yhat_noindia)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lb, ymax = ub), fill = rgb(186, 181, 213, maxColorValue = 255)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit), color = rgb(70, 55, 183, maxColorValue = 255), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = filter(df_2012_2024, india == 1), 
             aes(y = gdp_growth), 
             shape = 1, size = 4, color = "blue", stroke = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = filter(df_2012_2024, india == 1), 
            aes(y = gdp_growth, label = "India"), 
            hjust = -0.3, color = "black", size = 5) +
  labs(x = "Predicted Growth", y = "Actual Growth") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = rgb(242, 242, 242, maxColorValue = 255), color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Display the plot
print(plot_2012_2024)
```
